map_and_pairing: For p>1, t=p-1 and p'=2-p, the exact full-transpose spinflip J(X)=Y^tensor4 X^T Y^tensor4 satisfies Lambda_p=J Lambda_p'. J is linear, positive, trace-preserving, involutive, and self-adjoint for the complex trace pairing: Tr[Q J(X)]=Tr[J(Q)X]. It maps all actual complex rank-three orthogonal projectors bijectively to themselves as a set. Consequently a fixed-Q equality/strictness at p is equivalent to the SAME input and the single transformed projector J(Q) at p'. No partial-transpose positivity is invoked.
actual_product_top_spaces: If rho is the product of u_i and 0<t<1, then at p'=1-t the output's simple top vector is tensor_i u_i, with fourfold next eigenspace obtained by one local orthogonal flip. J maps those vectors to tensor_i (Y conjugate u_i) and its four one-factor orthogonal flips at p>1. Thus Q maximizes the p-output iff J(Q) contains the original product ray and has its remaining two dimensions in its one-flip space; equivalently Q contains the full-spinflipped product ray and selects two dimensions in its one-flip space. A pure product output has the reference spectrum, but an arbitrary Q need not attain it (erratum127).
